title: Beyond the Collections
blurb: The great works the famous lists never shelved — masterpieces Eliot and Adler overlooked, and the voices the old lists shut out.
about:
Every great-books list is also a list of exclusions. The Harvard Classics and the Great Books of the Western World were assembled by a few men with the tastes of their time — and they left out a great deal: almost every woman, most of the Romantic poets, the modern novel, and writers who didn't fit the mold.

Beyond the Collections is Lectio's correction — not a junk drawer of leftovers but a deliberate shelf of works that belong with the greatest and were simply missed: Sappho and Ovid, Murasaki's Western sisters, Frankenstein and Walden, Douglass and Dickinson, Proust and Woolf. The conversation the old lists started, continued by the voices they left out.

planned.title: The Poems of Sappho
planned.author: Sappho
planned.note: The greatest lyric poet of antiquity — fragments of desire and longing that still feel newly broken open.

planned.title: Metamorphoses
planned.author: Ovid
planned.note: Ovid's endlessly inventive epic of transformation — the myths the whole West would draw on forever.

planned.title: The Consolation of Philosophy
planned.author: Boethius
planned.note: Awaiting execution, Boethius is visited by Philosophy herself — the most read book of the Middle Ages after the Bible.

planned.title: The Decameron
planned.author: Giovanni Boccaccio
planned.note: A hundred tales told by ten young Florentines fleeing the plague — the birth of European prose fiction.

planned.title: In Praise of Folly
planned.author: Erasmus
planned.note: Erasmus lets Folly praise herself — the witty satire that lit the fuse of the Reformation.

planned.title: Tartuffe & The Misanthrope
planned.author: Molière
planned.note: The master of French comedy — hypocrisy and honesty skewered with perfect timing.

planned.title: Robinson Crusoe
planned.author: Daniel Defoe
planned.note: The castaway who built a world from nothing — often called the first English novel.

planned.title: Poems & The Reply to Sor Filotea
planned.author: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz
planned.note: The brilliant nun of colonial Mexico — and her fierce defense of a woman's right to learn.

planned.title: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
planned.author: Mary Wollstonecraft
planned.note: The founding work of feminist thought — reason and education are not the property of men.

planned.title: Songs of Innocence and of Experience
planned.author: William Blake
planned.note: Blake's visionary lyrics — the lamb and the tiger, innocence and its loss, in poems and his own engravings.

planned.title: Lyrical Ballads
planned.author: Wordsworth & Coleridge
planned.note: The book that began English Romanticism — ordinary life and the rime of the ancient mariner.

planned.title: Frankenstein
planned.author: Mary Shelley
planned.note: A teenager invents science fiction — the creature, its maker, and the terror of what we make.

planned.title: Eugene Onegin
planned.author: Alexander Pushkin
planned.note: Russia's beloved novel in verse — and the fountainhead of its entire literature.

planned.title: The Red and the Black
planned.author: Stendhal
planned.note: A carpenter's son claws toward the top of Restoration France — the first great psychological novel.

planned.title: Madame Bovary
planned.author: Gustave Flaubert
planned.note: A provincial wife dreams beyond her life — the novel that made prose an exact art.

planned.title: Les Misérables
planned.author: Victor Hugo
planned.note: An ex-convict's long redemption against the barricades of Paris — the great novel of mercy and justice.

planned.title: Walden
planned.author: Henry David Thoreau
planned.note: Two years alone at a pond — the American testament of simplicity and self-reliance.

planned.title: Leaves of Grass
planned.author: Walt Whitman
planned.note: Whitman sings America and himself — the barbaric yawp that remade what a poem could be.

planned.title: The Poems of Emily Dickinson
planned.author: Emily Dickinson
planned.note: Eighteen hundred tiny, electric poems on death, the soul, and the slant of light — published only after she died.

planned.title: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass
planned.author: Frederick Douglass
planned.note: The escaped slave who wrote his own freedom — the most powerful American memoir of the century.

planned.title: Jane Eyre
planned.author: Charlotte Brontë
planned.note: A governess who will not be owned — the novel that gave the heroine her own fierce voice.

planned.title: Wuthering Heights
planned.author: Emily Brontë
planned.note: Love as a force of nature on the Yorkshire moors — wild, strange, and unlike anything before it.

planned.title: In Search of Lost Time
planned.author: Marcel Proust
planned.note: Memory, time, and a taste of cake — the longest and deepest novel of the modern age.

planned.title: Mrs Dalloway
planned.author: Virginia Woolf
planned.note: One London day inside many minds — Woolf remakes the novel as the flow of consciousness.

planned.title: Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus
planned.author: Ludwig Wittgenstein
planned.note: Seven austere propositions on the limits of language — 'whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent.'

planned.title: Seven Pillars of Wisdom
planned.author: T. E. Lawrence
planned.note: Lawrence's first-hand epic of the Arab Revolt — guerrilla war across the desert, and the making and unmaking of a legend.

planned.title: The Stranger
planned.author: Albert Camus
planned.note: A man who feels nothing at his mother's funeral — the novel of the absurd that defined an era.

planned.title: The Second Sex
planned.author: Simone de Beauvoir
planned.note: 'One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman' — the foundation of modern feminist thought.

planned.author: George Orwell
planned.note: Big Brother, Newspeak, and the boot on the human face forever — the century's defining dystopia.

planned.title: The Old Man and the Sea
planned.author: Ernest Hemingway
planned.note: An old fisherman, a great marlin, and the dignity of struggle — Hemingway at his sparest.

planned.title: Waiting for Godot
planned.author: Samuel Beckett
planned.note: Two men wait for someone who never comes — the play that remade modern theater.

planned.title: Things Fall Apart
planned.author: Chinua Achebe
planned.note: An Igbo leader and the coming of the British — the novel that gave modern African literature its voice.

planned.title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
planned.author: Gabriel García Márquez
planned.note: The Buendía family across generations — the masterpiece of magical realism.

planned.title: Beloved
planned.author: Toni Morrison
planned.note: A mother, a ghost, and the unhealed wound of slavery — the great American novel of memory.
